key_insight: PRISA introduces a proactive roadside LiDAR framework that continuously monitors intersections to identify safety risks before they turn into crashes. It is designed to work in real-world conditions, including low light, while preserving privacy.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of safely monitoring complex urban intersections, where vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists interact in ways that can quickly lead to conflicts and crashes. Existing approaches often lack real-time, long-term, and privacy-preserving roadside sensing.
method: Uses modular infrastructure LiDAR sensors deployed at intersections for continuous observation of traffic scenes.
Focuses on proactive safety assessment by tracking multi-agent interactions and anticipating conflicts before escalation.
Designed for privacy-preserving and low-light-robust sensing to support long-term real-world deployment.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, PRISA shows how infrastructure sensing can move beyond detection toward predictive safety analytics in dynamic urban environments. It also highlights a practical deployment path for robust, privacy-aware perception systems.
visual_elements: Intersection diagram showing roadside LiDAR coverage zones and detected road users
Timeline or flowchart illustrating conflict prediction from observation to risk assessment
Icon set for vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists, privacy, and low-light conditions
Before/after graphic comparing reactive crash response vs proactive safety monitoring
paper_title: PRISA: Proactive Infrastructure LiDAR Framework for Intersection Safety Assessment
paper_authors: Tam Bang, Hussam Abubakr, Emiliano de la Garza Villarreal, Truc Phuong Nguyen, Austin Harris
